en.text:
Today’s M&A briefing — 2 deals, the strategies behind them · 22 October 2026

🔹 Data I/O (nasdaq-listed specialist in semiconductor programming, firmware loading systems into chips before integration) finalizes acquisition of V-TEK and A&J Programming (semiconductor handling, testing, packaging, and programming services) — $23m.
Data I/O anticipates doubling its revenue and reducing its dependence on automotive industry cycles. Mitch Jacobs, President of V-TEK, becomes Senior Vice President of Data I/O. The price includes $20 million in cash and $3 million in Data I/O shares.
Our view: The transaction shifts Data I/O from an automotive-focused model to a more recurring, on-demand programming model by expanding its industrial customer base and service capabilities.

🔹 Morgan Stanley Capital Partners (morgan Stanley Investment Management's middle-market buyout team) acquires The Rapid Group (TRG) (inspection, repair, and maintenance services for rotating equipment, pumps, motors, generators for municipal clients).
Founded over fifty years ago, TRG specializes in emergency maintenance of critical infrastructure, including some of the oldest water and wastewater networks in the United States, across six Northeastern states.
Our view: For MSCP, already invested in infrastructure services companies, the acquisition of TRG follows a regional consolidation logic: a dense platform in the Northeast, followed by geographic and capacity expansion through complementary acquisitions.

Data I/O anticipe un doublement de son chiffre d'affaires et une réduction de sa dépendance aux cycles de l'industrie automobile. Mitch Jacobs, président de V-TEK, devient vice-président senior de Data I/O.
Point de vue : L'opération déplace Data I/O d'un modèle concentré sur l'automobile vers un modèle plus récurrent — la programmation à la demande — en élargissant sa base de clients industriels et ses capacités de services.

🔹 Morgan Stanley Capital Partners (𝑒́𝑞𝑢𝑖𝑝𝑒 𝑑𝑒 𝑏𝑢𝑦𝑜𝑢𝑡 𝑚𝑖𝑑𝑑𝑙𝑒 𝑚𝑎𝑟𝑘𝑒𝑡 𝑑𝑒 𝑀𝑜𝑟𝑔𝑎𝑛 𝑆𝑡𝑎𝑛𝑙𝑒𝑦 𝐼𝑛𝑣𝑒𝑠𝑡𝑚𝑒𝑛𝑡 𝑀𝑎𝑛𝑎𝑔𝑒𝑚𝑒𝑛𝑡) rachète The Rapid Group (TRG) (𝑠𝑒𝑟𝑣𝑖𝑐𝑒𝑠 𝑑'𝑖𝑛𝑠𝑝𝑒𝑐𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛, 𝑟𝑒́𝑝𝑎𝑟𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑒𝑡 𝑚𝑎𝑖𝑛𝑡𝑒𝑛𝑎𝑛𝑐𝑒 𝑑'𝑒́𝑞𝑢𝑖𝑝𝑒𝑚𝑒𝑛𝑡𝑠 𝑟𝑜𝑡𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑓𝑠, 𝑝𝑜𝑚𝑝𝑒𝑠, 𝑚𝑜𝑡𝑒𝑢𝑟𝑠, 𝑔𝑒́𝑛𝑒́𝑟𝑎𝑡𝑒𝑢𝑟𝑠 𝑝𝑜𝑢𝑟 𝑐𝑙𝑖𝑒𝑛𝑡𝑠 𝑚𝑢𝑛𝑖𝑐𝑖𝑝𝑎𝑢𝑥).
Fondée il y a plus de cinquante ans, TRG est spécialisée dans la maintenance d'urgence d'infrastructures critiques, notamment les réseaux d'eau et d'eaux usées parmi les plus anciens des États-Unis, dans six États du Nord-Est.
Point de vue : Pour MSCP, déjà investi dans des sociétés de services aux infrastructures, l'acquisition de TRG suit une logique de consolidation régionale : une plateforme dense dans le Nord-Est, puis une extension géographique et capacitaire par acquisitions complémentaires.

en.text:
Today’s fundraising briefing — 8 deals, the strategies behind them · 22 October 2026

🔹 Fundbot — more than $500m · Seed.
Founded in 2020, Fundbot claims over $500 million in financing granted to more than 3,000 SMEs. The total raised since 2023 reaches $2.6 million.
Investors: Middle East Venture Partners (MEVP) and Salica Investment (re-investors); Hub71, Abu Dhabi tech hub (new entrant).
Our view: Hub71's presence in this round signals an ambition to expand into the Gulf, consistent with a model that operates where traditional banks do not—SMEs in markets perceived as risky.

🔹 Pigment (financial and operational planning platform for finance, HR, and operations teams: forecasting models) — $250m · Series E.
Founded in 2019, Pigment directly competes with Anaplan (acquired by Thoma Bravo), Adaptive Insights (Workday), and Planful. Valuation has increased since the previous round.
Investors: Scaleup Europe Fund (lead investor); Nvidia.
Our view: Nvidia's presence in the round signals that Pigment integrates or plans to integrate high-performance computing capabilities into its models, and provides a credibility signal in the US market where the battle against established players is fought as much on technology as on partner reputation.

🔹 Eka Robotics — $150m · Series A.
This round offers insight into how Andreessen Horowitz intends to use its $1.1 billion hardware fund.
Investors: Andreessen Horowitz and F-Prime (co-lead investors).
Our view: Eka bets that vertical integration—hand and force model in the same product—creates sustainable differentiation against purely visual approaches, by solving the main bottleneck of industrial robotics: fine dexterity.

🔹 Dream Labs (foundational model, Dream-1 trained on human interactions to control any two-armed robotic system equipped with grippers) — $90m · Seed.
Dream Labs emerges from stealth with this round. Within twenty-four hours of Dream-1's launch, the model was used to control 31 types of robots it had never encountered during training.
Use of funds: Compute funding to expand task library and increase model scale.

🔹 ExponTech (distributed data storage for enterprise IT infrastructure in China, with a KV Cache product, WQS optimized) — more than $13.8m.

🔹 EstateMin (AI tool for law firms specializing in estate and trust law, founded in 2024, based in New York) — €1m · Pre-seed.
Founded in 2024, EstateMin was initially Irish before moving to New York. The company reports 20% monthly revenue growth.

🔹 Biogenera (italian biotech based near Bologna developing anti-gene drugs via the patented MyGenera platform) — €667,469. Fundraising in progress — target amount, not yet closed.

🔹 Momentum Technologies (manufacturer of survival capsules under the LifePods brand: anti-ballistic version, B01, ICC 500 certified) — €400,000. Fundraising in progress — target amount, not yet closed.

Levées de fonds : les 8 opérations chiffrées de l'édito du 22 octobre 2026.

🔹 Fundbot — plus de 500 M$ · Seed.
Fondée en 2020, Fundbot revendique plus de 500 millions de dollars de financements accordés à plus de 3 000 PME. Le total levé depuis 2023 atteint 2,6 millions de dollars.
Avec : Middle East Venture Partners (MEVP) et Salica Investment (réinvestisseurs) ; Hub71, hub tech d'Abu Dhabi (nouvel entrant).
Point de vue : La présence de Hub71 dans ce tour signale une ambition d'extension vers le Golfe, cohérente avec un modèle qui opère là où les banques traditionnelles ne vont pas — des PME dans des marchés perçus comme risqués.

🔹 Pigment (𝑝𝑙𝑎𝑡𝑒𝑓𝑜𝑟𝑚𝑒 𝑑𝑒 𝑝𝑙𝑎𝑛𝑖𝑓𝑖𝑐𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑓𝑖𝑛𝑎𝑛𝑐𝑖𝑒̀𝑟𝑒 𝑒𝑡 𝑜𝑝𝑒́𝑟𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛𝑛𝑒𝑙𝑙𝑒 𝑝𝑜𝑢𝑟 𝑒́𝑞𝑢𝑖𝑝𝑒𝑠 𝑓𝑖𝑛𝑎𝑛𝑐𝑒) — 250 M$ · Série E.
Fondée en 2019, Pigment concurrence directement Anaplan (racheté par Thoma Bravo), Adaptive Insights (Workday) et Planful. La valorisation a progressé par rapport au tour précédent.
Avec : Scaleup Europe Fund (chef de file) ; Nvidia.
Point de vue : La présence de Nvidia au tour signale que Pigment intègre ou prévoit d'intégrer des capacités de calcul intensif dans ses modèles, et constitue un signal de crédibilité sur le marché américain où la bataille contre les acteurs établis se joue autant sur la technologie que sur la réputation des partenaires.

🔹 Eka Robotics — 150 M$ · Série A.
Ce tour donne un aperçu de l'usage qu'Andreessen Horowitz entend faire de son fonds hardware de 1,1 milliard de dollars.
Avec : Andreessen Horowitz et F-Prime (co-chefs de file).
Point de vue : Eka parie que l'intégration verticale — main et modèle de force dans un même produit — crée une différenciation durable face aux approches purement visuelles, en résolvant le verrou principal de la robotique industrielle : la dextérité fine.

🔹 Dream Labs (𝑚𝑜𝑑𝑒̀𝑙𝑒 𝑓𝑜𝑛𝑑𝑎𝑡𝑒𝑢𝑟, 𝐷𝑟𝑒𝑎𝑚-1 𝑒𝑛𝑡𝑟𝑎𝑖̂𝑛𝑒́ 𝑠𝑢𝑟 𝑑𝑒𝑠 𝑖𝑛𝑡𝑒𝑟𝑎𝑐𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛𝑠 ℎ𝑢𝑚𝑎𝑖𝑛𝑒𝑠) — 90 M$ · Seed.
Avec : B Capital et Kindred Ventures (co-chefs de file).

🔹 ExponTech (𝑠𝑡𝑜𝑐𝑘𝑎𝑔𝑒 𝑑𝑒 𝑑𝑜𝑛𝑛𝑒́𝑒𝑠 𝑑𝑖𝑠𝑡𝑟𝑖𝑏𝑢𝑒́ 𝑝𝑜𝑢𝑟 𝑖𝑛𝑓𝑟𝑎𝑠𝑡𝑟𝑢𝑐𝑡𝑢𝑟𝑒 𝐼𝑇 𝑑'𝑒𝑛𝑡𝑟𝑒𝑝𝑟𝑖𝑠𝑒 𝑒𝑛 𝐶ℎ𝑖𝑛𝑒) — plus de 13,8 M$.

🔹 EstateMin (𝑜𝑢𝑡𝑖𝑙 𝐼𝐴 𝑝𝑜𝑢𝑟 𝑐𝑎𝑏𝑖𝑛𝑒𝑡𝑠 𝑑'𝑎𝑣𝑜𝑐𝑎𝑡𝑠 𝑠𝑝𝑒́𝑐𝑖𝑎𝑙𝑖𝑠𝑒́𝑠 𝑒𝑛 𝑑𝑟𝑜𝑖𝑡 𝑑𝑒𝑠 𝑠𝑢𝑐𝑐𝑒𝑠𝑠𝑖𝑜𝑛𝑠 𝑒𝑡 𝑑𝑒𝑠 𝑡𝑟𝑢𝑠𝑡𝑠) — 1 M€ · Pré-seed.

🔹 Biogenera (𝑏𝑖𝑜𝑡𝑒𝑐ℎ 𝑖𝑡𝑎𝑙𝑖𝑒𝑛 𝑏𝑎𝑠𝑒́ 𝑝𝑟𝑒̀𝑠 𝑑𝑒 𝐵𝑜𝑙𝑜𝑔𝑛𝑒 𝑑𝑒́𝑣𝑒𝑙𝑜𝑝𝑝𝑎𝑛𝑡 𝑑𝑒𝑠 𝑚𝑒́𝑑𝑖𝑐𝑎𝑚𝑒𝑛𝑡𝑠 𝑎𝑛𝑡𝑖-𝑔𝑒̀𝑛𝑒) — 667 469 €. Levée en cours — montant visé, non encore bouclé.
